title: Platform standup: rotations, fallthroughs, and quota headroom - Mar 9 2027
content:
Attendees: Anika (owner), Marcus, Priya, Omar, Ella, Jae (brief join).

Purpose: weekly sync focused on control plane handoffs, routing experiments (fallthrough behavior), auth token churn, and quota headroom planning for Dedicated customers. Quick decisions + action owners. Notes are rough; TODOs at the bottom.

AGENDA SUMMARY
- Quick health check (metrics / incidents)
- Routing: fallthroughs vs retries for high-latency pools
- Auth: token refresh race on private deployments
- Quotas: headroom and burst policies for committed capacity
- Rollouts: allocator canary progress and canary metrics to watch
- Blockers / triage items

1) HEALTH CHECK
- No Sev1s since last Tuesday. Small flurry of 5xx spikes Fri 03/05 tied to a misconfigured proxy route (fixed by infra team).
- Key metric snapshots (running 03/09 morning):
  - Control-plane P95 API latency (create/deploy): 210ms (goal  < 150ms for non-bulk ops)
  - Routing rejection rate (fallback to hosted variant): 0.8% yesterday, transient spikes to 2.5% during eu-west-1 Maintenance window
  - Auth refresh failures: 0.12% (mostly private-deployments with older cert rotation code)
  - Quota throttle events: 3 customers hit hard throttle yesterday (all on Dedicated, billing/ops notified)
- Notes: P95 on control-plane elevated because of a small regression in validation code (PR referenced below). Marcus will prioritize a follow-up micro-optimization.

2) ROUTING / FALLTHROUGH STRATEGY (lead: Marcus)
- Context: we have two behaviors when a preferred routing pool is overloaded or slow: fallthrough to cheaper/compatible variant OR retry against the same pool. Current policy is fallthrough-first for latency-sensitive routes, retry-first for consistency-sensitive flows.
- Recent experiments: multi-step fallthrough that prefers region-local cheaper variants then cross-region:
  - Experiment window: 03/02 - 03/07 (traffic split 5%)
  - Observed: 7% lower successful latency tail vs retries-first for short-lived prompts, but slight uptick in token cost (~1.4%) due to longer model paths in fallback
- Decision: keep experiment active but change threshold triggers:
  - If pool latency > 350ms for two consecutive s-seconds, trigger fallthrough (was 500ms).
  - Add tag-based exception: "no-fallthrough" for customers who opt-in to strict model alignment.
- Action: Marcus to update routing-policy-config and push a feature flag (FF: route_fallthrough_tighter) by 03/12. Add a metric for fallthrough-initiated percentage per-customer.

3) AUTH / TOKEN ROTATION (lead: Priya)
- Problem: private deployments with older rotation agent see a token race where multiple agents request new tokens concurrently causing transient 401s. Symptoms show up as 401 spikes during customer-managed cron jobs and cert rotations.
- Root cause hypothesis: rotation agent doesn't coordinate and uses an in-memory lock; in k8s sidecar scenarios the lock is per-pod not cluster-scoped.
- Proposed fix paths:
  - Short-term: add jitter + backoff to rotation requests and increase tolerance window (Priya to ship hotfix 03/11).
  - Medium-term: implement a cluster-scoped coordination (etcd lease or KMS-based leader election) — tracked in INF-2402.
- Customer impact: two private customers reported transient failures (support tickets 14892, 14907). Both notified and given mitigation steps (restart sidecar or increase retry window).
- Action: Priya to publish KB in support playbooks with exact mitigation steps by 03/10 and send note to Solutions engineering.

4) QUOTAS / HEADROOM (lead: Omar)
- Observations: quota throttle events concentrated on a small set of Dedicated customers after autoscale bursts. Current quota windows are conservative.
- Proposal: add "burst headroom" for committed customers that allows temporary +20% capacity for up to 10 minutes with downstream cost-metering and alerts. This avoids immediate throttles while preserving long-term capacity constraints.
- Risks: could hide underprovisioning; needs clear billing signals and Ops guardrails.
- Action items:
  - Omar to draft policy doc (burstable headroom + billing signals) and share with finance + SRE by 03/16 (JIRA INF-2415).
  - Ella to prototype alerting playbook so on-call sees "burst headroom used" vs "hard throttle". Prototype by 03/15.

5) ALLOCATOR CANARY / ROLLOUT (lead: Ella)
- Canary PR merged (GH PR 412), canary in prod serving 2% of routing traffic. Initial metrics look good but:
  - Observed slightly higher KV cache miss rate in canary (3.1% vs 2.4% control) — likely due to a mis-sized cache config.
  - Memory footprint +4% on canary nodes (within limits for now).
- Next steps: adjust canary cache size and re-run A/B for 48h. If KV miss improves, expand to 10% on Mon 03/15.
- Action: Ella to open follow-up PR to tweak cache defaults and include regression test in allocator unit harness.

6) BLOCKERS / TRIAGE
- INF-2387: validation regression in control-plane that slows deploy path for multi-file models. Marcus assigned, in-progress. Target patch 03/11.
- INF-2379: quota metering discrepancy for usage window crossing DST boundary — finance flagged possible billing inaccuracies. Omar + Finance to investigate.
- Oncall notes: rotate schedule mismatch last week — small confusion during handover (Anika to propose a simpler weekly rota view in Confluence).

7) SMALL OP NOTES / RANDOMS
- Reminder: dark-launch of new tracing headers next week (add to rollout calendar).
- Takeaway from SRE review: add a lightweight synthetic that hits control-plane create/deploy path at 30s cadence to catch P95 regressions sooner. Jae volunteered to wire this.
- Notes-to-self: keep an eye on eu-west-1 fallthrough rate as the regional maintenance window recurs.

ACTIONS (owner - due)
- Marcus: Fix validation regression micro-optimizations and land INF-2387 patch (03/11).
- Marcus: Implement FF route_fallthrough_tighter + expose per-customer fallthrough metric (03/12).
- Priya: Hotfix for rotation agent with jitter/backoff + publish KB (03/11 for hotfix, 03/10 KB).
- Omar: Draft burst headroom policy & JIRA INF-2415 (03/16).
- Ella: Follow-up PR for allocator cache defaults + run 48h AB (03/12).
- Anika: Publish simplified oncall rota view in Confluence (03/13).
- Jae: Instrument control-plane synthetic (start 03/12).

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Do we apply burst headroom by default to all committed tiers or only to those that opt-in? (Ops + Finance weigh-in requested).
- How aggressive should the fallthrough thresholds be for low-latency endpoints vs routing stability?

REFERENCE LINKS / NOTES
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/412
- JIRA: INF-2387 (validation regression), INF-2402 (auth rotation coordination), INF-2415 (quota headroom policy)
- Slack thread: #pltfm-routing: t2b3f4 (experiment logs and trace snippets)

END NOTES
- This doc is a working capture. If you want more details or raw logs I pulled a few queries into the #pltfm-routing thread.
- Ping me if you want a short summary for the exec update — can produce a 1-slide snapshot.

-- Anika
